title: Reaction rate - 123 school
heading: Reaction rate
intro: You learn these terms and calculations by practising. Only use BINAS when the question names a BINAS table.

questions.question: What is the reaction rate?

answers.a: How fast the reactants disappear and the new substances are formed
answers.b: How much heat is released in the reaction
answers.c: At what temperature the reaction takes place

questions.question: What is the reaction time?

answers.c: How much heat is released in the reaction
answers.d: How much substance is left at the end

questions.question: A reaction goes faster. What happens to the reaction time?

answers.b: The reaction time stays the same

questions.question: What happens to the reaction rate if you raise the temperature?

answers.b: The reaction rate stays the same

questions.question: What happens to the reaction rate if you lower the temperature?

answers.c: The reaction rate stays the same

questions.question: What happens to the reaction rate if you increase the concentration of a reactant?

answers.b: The reaction rate stays the same

questions.question: You make a solid finer, for example powder instead of a lump (greater degree of division). What happens to the reaction rate?

answers.a: The reaction rate stays the same

questions.question: In a reaction between gases you increase the pressure. What happens to the reaction rate?

answers.b: The reaction rate stays the same

questions.question: What does a catalyst do?

answers.a: It speeds up the reaction and is used up at the end
answers.c: It has no effect on the reaction
answers.d: It speeds up the reaction and is not used up at the end

questions.question: You raise the temperature. What happens to the reaction time?

answers.b: The reaction time stays the same

questions.question: You add a catalyst. What happens to the reaction time?

answers.a: The reaction time stays the same

questions.question: You increase the concentration of a reactant. What happens to the reaction time?

answers.d: The reaction time stays the same

questions.question: Does the type of substance affect the reaction rate?

answers.a: Yes, but only at a high temperature
answers.b: No, all reactions go equally fast
answers.d: Yes, some substances naturally react faster than others

questions.question: Which of these things affects the reaction rate?
You see a graph of the amount of reactant against time. The line slopes steeply downwards. What does that mean?

answers.c: The reaction has not started yet

questions.question: Name three factors that affect the reaction rate.

answers.a: The colour, smell and taste of the substances
answers.b: The name of the substance, the make and the price
answers.c: The mass of the beaker, the time of day and the place
answers.d: For example the temperature, the concentration and the degree of division

questions.question: An effervescent tablet dissolves faster in warm water than in cold water. Which factor is responsible?
Why does a powder react faster than a lump of the same substance?

answers.b: A powder has a much larger surface area, so more particles can react at the same time
answers.c: A powder has a higher temperature
answers.d: A powder is a different substance

questions.question: Small wood shavings catch fire faster than a large log. Which factor is responsible?
Why do you store food in the fridge?

answers.a: A catalyst works in the fridge
answers.b: In the fridge the concentration of the food is higher
answers.c: At a low temperature every reaction stops for good
answers.d: At a low temperature the spoilage reactions are slower

questions.question: Why is flour dust dangerous in a flour mill?

answers.a: The dust has an enormous degree of division and can then react explosively with oxygen
answers.c: Flour only reacts at a low temperature
answers.d: Flour is a very heavy substance

questions.question: A wood splinter burns much faster in pure oxygen than in air. Which factor is responsible?

answers.b: The concentration of oxygen is higher
answers.c: The temperature of the wood is lower
answers.d: The degree of division of the wood is smaller

questions.question: A catalytic converter in a car makes sure that poisonous carbon monoxide is converted quickly. Which factor is used here?

answers.a: The degree of division of the petrol

questions.question: You add a catalyst. How much product is formed in the end?

answers.a: The same amount as without a catalyst, but faster
answers.d: No product is formed any more

questions.question: What is an enzyme?

answers.d: A substance that stops a reaction

questions.question: You let 5.0 g of zinc react with an excess of hydrochloric acid, first at 20 °C and then at 40 °C. What is different at 40 °C?

answers.d: The reaction is finished sooner, the same amount of hydrogen is formed

questions.question: Magnesium reacts with 2 mol/L hydrochloric acid and with 0.5 mol/L hydrochloric acid. In which solution does the reaction go fastest?
In a reaction 60 mL of gas is formed in 30 seconds. What is the average reaction rate?
Which two ways are useful for measuring the reaction rate when a gas is formed?

answers.a: Write down the density of the solution from memory
answers.b: Look at the colour of the beaker
answers.c: Measure the gas volume per time, or measure the decrease in mass per time
answers.d: Look up the name of the gas

questions.question: Why does the reaction rate usually become smaller over time?

answers.d: The reactants are being used up, so the concentration becomes smaller

questions.question: In a graph of the amount of product against time, the line becomes horizontal after a while. What does that mean?

answers.b: The reaction has not started yet
answers.c: The reaction has finished, a reactant is used up

questions.question: You measure the reaction twice with the same amount of reactant. Line B rises more steeply than line A. Which statement is correct?

answers.a: The reaction of B is slower
answers.b: More product is eventually formed in B
answers.c: The reaction of B is faster, but B ends at the same height as A
answers.d: Less product is eventually formed in B

questions.question: Name two ways to make a reaction go more slowly.

answers.b: Lower the temperature and reduce the concentration
answers.c: Make the substance finer and increase the pressure
answers.d: Raise the temperature and add a catalyst
